newsitem.title: UGANDA: Cen bank intervenes to stem Uganda shilling fall.
newsitem.headline: Cen bank intervenes to stem Uganda shilling fall.

text.p: The central Bank of Uganda sold $3 million in the foreign exchange market in April to support the local currency, the bank said on Wednesday.

It said in a monthly report that the shilling eased 2.1 percent in April from March "largely due to a shortage of dollars in the market". It said the bank sold dollars to commercial banks to help ease the tight supply situation.
That was a reversal of the shilling'S performance in February and March, when it posted gains of 1.1 percent and 0.8 percent respectively, according to available central bank data.
The shilling interbank commercial mean was posted at 1046.46 versus the dollar in April compared to 1024.95 in March.

The central bank offered no reason for the shilling fall against the dollar other than the tight supply situation. But dealers said part of the problem was that the coffee season was taparing off around April, which meant a scarcity of dollars.
Coffee is Uganda's dominant foreign exchange earner.

There was a slight decline in the volume of transactions in the interbank market, with gross foreign exchange purchases falling to $111.01 million in April from $112.96 million in March. Gross sales rose to $117.01 million from $109.12 million in the same period, according to the report.

Money supply (M2) grew by 2.2 percent to 663.3 billion shillings in February 1997 compared to 649.3 billion shillings at end-January 1996. The bank blamed the increase on a rise in net domestic credit, which reached 300.2 billion at end-Fenruary 1997 against 276.6 billion shillings in January 1996.

Currency in circulation declined by 1.3 billion shillings to 225 billion at February 1997 compared to February 1996 while demand deposits increased by 9.1 billion to 229.1 billion shillings in the same period, the central bank said.
The bank offered no predictions for May.
